raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Tokenize a long text prompt as pieces in one tokenizer call, so that the Rust tokenizer encodes the pieces on all CPU threads. For a 1M-token prompt with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, the render request takes 0.30 s instead of 1.64 s, and the token IDs are the same. #45514, #47583 and #48544 are related, but they do something else (see Details).

## Claims

- `POST /v1/completions/render` with a 1M-token prompt takes 295 ms instead of 1637 ms on a 16-core CPU. With two such requests at the same time, the slower one takes 620 ms instead of 3157 ms. The prompt is tokenized before the request reaches the engine, so this time comes off the time to first token.
- The token IDs are the same as those of the normal tokenizer call, also with truncation on the left or the right side.
- Tokenizers, arguments and texts that this does not handle go through the normal call as before.

## Validation

Unit tests on CPU:

```bash
pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_parallel_encode.py tests/renderers/test_completions.py
```

All 65 tests pass: 28 new tests in `tests/tokenizers_/test_parallel_encode.py`, and 37 tests in `tests/renderers/test_completions.py`, 2 of them new. The new tests compare the token IDs with the normal call on 3M characters of mixed text for `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`. They also cut a 262K-character text at each of its more than 20,000 cut places, check truncation on both sides, call the thread-pool tokenizer of the renderer from 4 threads, and check that unsupported tokenizers, configurations and arguments use the normal call. The renderer tests check that the renderer takes the new path and that a prompt that is too long still fails the length check.

Outside CI, I compared the token IDs for `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B` and `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B` on 28 texts: 24 random mixed texts of 0.3M to 1.2M characters, 4M characters of `vllm/**/*.py`, 2M characters of `docs/**/*.md`, and the `vocab.json` and `merges.txt` of Qwen3. All 112 results are the same as the normal call, and so are the token IDs of the pieces cut at each of the 10.3M cut places. `vocab.json` has no cut place, so it used the normal call.

End to end, I started the render server on main and on this PR:

```bash
VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 vllm launch render Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 8199 --max-model-len 1048576
```

The client sends `{"model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "prompt": text}` to `/v1/completions/render` and measures the time until the response with the token IDs arrives. `text` is the first 4,533,131 characters of `vllm/**/*.py` in path order, which is exactly 1,000,000 tokens. The 1,000,000 token IDs from the server with this PR are the same as those of `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B")(text)`.

| 1M-token prompt | main (`9e2b579aabe9`) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| one request at a time, median of 6 | 1637 ms (1583 to 1661) | 295 ms (277 to 311) |
| two requests at the same time, slower request, median of 3 pairs | 3157 ms | 620 ms |

The CPU is an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X with 16 cores and 32 threads. The packages are tokenizers 0.23.3 and transformers 5.19.0.

<details>
<summary>Tokenizer call only, by prompt length</summary>

This is the same text and tokenizer, with the median of 5 calls in one process. The last column is the call that this PR makes.

| characters | tokens | pieces | normal call | pieces |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 65,536 | 17,540 | 1 | 11.1 ms | 11.2 ms |
| 131,072 | 33,791 | 2 | 21.9 ms | 12.5 ms |
| 262,144 | 66,787 | 4 | 51.5 ms | 15.5 ms |
| 524,288 | 126,213 | 8 | 126.6 ms | 24.3 ms |
| 1,048,576 | 241,893 | 16 | 287.7 ms | 42.5 ms |
| 2,097,152 | 475,901 | 32 | 654.0 ms | 85.2 ms |
| 4,533,131 | 1,000,000 | 70 | 1504.8 ms | 194.3 ms |

With `TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false`, the 1M-token prompt takes 1526 ms with the normal call and 1089 ms as pieces. The pieces are then encoded one after another, and they are still faster because the normal call gets slower per token as the text grows, from 0.63 µs per token at 65,536 characters to 1.5 µs per token at 4.5M characters.

The check of a tokenizer runs once per tokenizer object and took 1.4 ms.

</details>

This PR includes no GPU serving benchmark. The change only affects the tokenizer call in the API server, which the render server runs in the same way, and the engine gets the same token IDs as before, so the model output does not change.

## Details

`BaseRenderer._tokenize_prompt` calls the new `try_parallel_encode` before the normal tokenizer call. It returns `None` for a prompt of fewer than 262,144 characters, for a request that needs token offsets, for encode arguments other than `add_special_tokens`, `truncation` and `max_length`, and for an unsupported tokenizer. The renderer then makes the normal call.

The text is cut into pieces of at least 65,536 characters, and each piece ends at a cut place: before a space, or after a line break, where an ASCII letter or digit follows. With the pre-tokenizer regex of Qwen2 to Qwen3, and the one of Qwen3.5 and later, a space in front of a letter or digit always starts a pre-token, and no alternative runs from a line break into a letter or digit. The regexes also find the same pre-tokens in a piece as in the whole text, because they have no lookbehind, and their one lookahead, `(?!\S)` after a run of whitespace, gives the same result at the end of a piece as in the whole text. BPE merges never cross a pre-token, so the token IDs of the pieces, put one after the other, are the token IDs of the whole text.

A tokenizer is supported when:

- it is a `TokenizersBackend` with a Rust `tokenizers.Tokenizer`,
- the normalizer is NFC or none,
- the pre-tokenizer is a `Split` with one of the two regexes (`Isolated`, not inverted), followed by `ByteLevel` without `add_prefix_space` and `use_regex`,
- the model is BPE without dropout, and the post-processor is `ByteLevel` or none,
- no added token has `lstrip`, `rstrip`, `single_word` or a cut place inside its content,
- and the normal call on a short sample gives the same token IDs as the sample cut at every cut place, with and without special tokens. This catches a tokenizer class that changes the text or adds tokens in Python.

The result is cached per tokenizer object in a `WeakKeyDictionary`. The pieces are encoded with the public call `tokenizer(pieces, add_special_tokens=False, return_attention_mask=False)`, so they go through the thread-pool wrapper from #41181 like every other call. Truncation is applied to the result on the truncation side of the tokenizer, as the normal call does.

This PR does not duplicate an open PR. #45514 adds an opt-in tokenizer mode that splits the text on a special-token delimiter, so it does not help a long document without that token. #47583 adds an opt-in cache that reuses the encoding of the previous turn of a multi-turn chat. It also hooks `_tokenize_prompt`, and the two compose, because a cache miss can go to this path. #48544 batches many offline prompts into one call, and it does not split one long prompt.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- A long prompt uses all threads of the Rust thread pool for about 0.2 s per 1M tokens. Two long prompts at the same time share that pool, as the second row of the table shows.
- Only the two Qwen regexes are on the list. Other regexes, for example those of Llama 3 or DeepSeek V3, need the same argument before they can be added to `_SPLIT_REGEXES`.
- A text with no cut place, such as CJK text without ASCII words, uses the normal call.

AI assistance was used for this PR.

nodes.body: This is already what fastokens does

I checked `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` with fastokens 0.3.4 on the 1M-token prompt of this PR. It also cuts the prompt at pre-token boundaries and encodes the chunks in parallel, its token IDs are the same for Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-0.8B, and it is faster than this PR at every prompt length in the description. So I am closing this PR.

The fastokens package is not in the vLLM Docker images, so `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` raises an ImportError there (#47855). Is there a plan to add it? #47859 and #47863 got no review.
@maeehart yes I think we can get it added to the image by default.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

files.patch:
@@ -16,6 +16,8 @@
 from vllm.renderers import TokenizeParams
 from vllm.renderers.hf import HfRenderer
 from vllm.renderers.inputs.preprocess import parse_model_prompt, prompt_to_seq
+from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer
+from vllm.tokenizers.parallel_encode import try_parallel_encode
 
 MODEL_NAME = "openai-community/gpt2"
 
@@ -766,3 +768,67 @@ def test_both_prompts_and_embeds(self):
         assert len(results[0]["prompt_token_ids"]) == len(text_input)
         # Second should be embed prompt
         assert torch.equal(results[1]["prompt_embeds"], tensor_input)
+
+
+LONG_PROMPT_MODEL_NAME = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
+# 306,000 characters and about 70k tokens, long enough for the renderer to
+# tokenize the prompt in parallel pieces.
+LONG_PROMPT = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog 12345.\n" * 6000
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def long_prompt_tokenizer():
+    return get_tokenizer(LONG_PROMPT_MODEL_NAME, truncation_side="left")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def parallel_results(monkeypatch) -> list:
+    """Record what `try_parallel_encode` returns to the renderer."""
+    results: list = []
+
+    def spy(*args):
+        results.append(token_ids := try_parallel_encode(*args))
+        return token_ids
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr("vllm.renderers.base.try_parallel_encode", spy)
+    return results
+
+
+def _tokenize_long_prompt(tokenizer, params: TokenizeParams):
+    model_config = MockModelConfig(
+        model=LONG_PROMPT_MODEL_NAME, tokenizer=LONG_PROMPT_MODEL_NAME
+    )
+    renderer = HfRenderer(
+        MockVllmConfig(model_config, parallel_config=MockParallelConfig()),
+        tokenizer=tokenizer,
+    )
+    prompts = renderer.render_prompts(_preprocess_prompt(model_config, LONG_PROMPT))
+    return renderer.tokenize_prompts(prompts, params)
+
+
+class TestTokenizeLongPrompt:
+    """A long text prompt is tokenized in parallel pieces. The token IDs must
+    be the same as those of the normal tokenizer call."""
+
+    def test_truncation(self, long_prompt_tokenizer, parallel_results):
+        tokenizer = long_prompt_tokenizer
+        results = _tokenize_long_prompt(
+            tokenizer,
+            TokenizeParams(max_total_tokens=200_000, truncate_prompt_tokens=1000),
+        )
+        assert parallel_results[0] is not None
+        # The tokenizer truncates on the left side.
+        expected = tokenizer(LONG_PROMPT)["input_ids"][-1000:]
+        assert results[0]["prompt_token_ids"] == expected
+
+    def test_too_long(self, long_prompt_tokenizer, parallel_results):
+        tokenizer = long_prompt_tokenizer
+        # The limit lets the text pass the length check in characters, so
+        # the error comes from the length check in tokens.
+        limit = len(LONG_PROMPT) // tokenizer.max_chars_per_token + 1
+        assert limit < len(tokenizer(LONG_PROMPT)["input_ids"])
+        with pytest.raises(
+            VLLMValidationError, match=f"at least {limit + 1} input tokens"
+        ):
+            _tokenize_long_prompt(tokenizer, TokenizeParams(max_total_tokens=limit))
+        assert parallel_results[0] is not None

@@ -0,0 +1,332 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests that a long prompt tokenized in parallel pieces gets the same token
+IDs as the normal tokenizer call, and that other cases use the normal call."""
+
+import copy
+import itertools
+import json
+import random
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+
+import pytest
+from tokenizers import Tokenizer, pre_tokenizers
+from transformers import TokenizersBackend
+
+from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer
+from vllm.tokenizers.hf import maybe_make_thread_pool
+from vllm.tokenizers.parallel_encode import (
+    _CUT_PATTERN,
+    MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS,
+    _cut_into_pieces,
+    _encode_pieces,
+    try_parallel_encode,
+)
+
+# Qwen3 uses the pre-tokenizer regex of Qwen2 to Qwen3. Qwen3.5 uses the regex
+# that also puts combining marks into words.
+QWEN_TOKENIZERS = ["Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", "Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B"]
+
+# The keyword arguments that `TokenizeParams.get_encode_kwargs` gives when the
+# prompt is not truncated.
+NO_TRUNCATION = {"truncation": False, "max_length": None, "add_special_tokens": True}
+
+# Words and snippets for the test text. They put cut places next to special
+# tokens, digits, punctuation, CJK and other scripts, emojis, combining marks
+# and line breaks, and they add places that look like cut places but are not
+# ones, such as a letter after a tab, a no-break space or a next-line char.
+WORDS = [
+    "the", "quick", "brown", "fox", "jumps", "over", "lazy", "dog", "A", "I",
+    "x", "vLLM", "Qwen", "tokenizer", "prompt", "don't", "it's", "we'll",
+    "I'm", "they're", "café", "naïve", "über", "Straße", "résumé", "ﬁle",
+    "e\u0301t\u0301e\u0301", "0", "7", "42", "3.14159", "2026-10-14", "1,000,000",
+    "12345678901234567890", "0x1F", "v1.2.3", "x86_64", "GPU0",
+]  # fmt: skip
+SNIPPETS = [
+    "\n", "\r\n", "\r", "\n\n", "\n\n\n", "\t", "  ", "   ", " \n", "\n ",
+    "\n\t", "\t\n", " \r\n ", ".", ",", "!", "?", "...", " - ", "--", "(", ")",
+    "[x]", '{"a": 1, "b": [2, 3]}', " #", " //", "'s", "'ll", " '", "\"",
+    "<|im_start|>", "<|im_end|>", "<|endoftext|>", "<think>", "</think>",
+    "<tool_call>", "</tool_call>", "<|im_start", "im_end|>", "<|im_start|>user\n",
+    "<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n", "中文分词测试", " 日本語のテキスト",
+    "한국어 문장", " مرحبا", " שלום", " Ελληνικά", " Привет мир", "😀", " 👍🏽",
+    "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦", " 🇫🇮", "\u0301", " \u0301x", "\u00a0A", "\u3000B", "\u2028C",
+    "\x85D", "\x0bE", "\tF", "def f(x):\n    return x + 1\n",
+    "for i in range(10):\n\tprint(i)\n", "https://example.com/a?b=c&d=1",
+    "\n1. First\n2. Second\n", "\nThe end.\n",
+]  # fmt: skip
+
+
+def make_text(num_chars: int, seed: int = 0) -> str:
+    """Return a random text of about `num_chars` characters."""
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    parts: list[str] = []
+    length = 0
+    while length < num_chars:
+        part = " " + rng.choice(WORDS) if rng.random() < 0.7 else rng.choice(SNIPPETS)
+        parts.append(part)
+        length += len(part)
+    return "".join(parts)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def long_text() -> str:
+    return make_text(3_000_000)
+
+
+_loaded: dict[tuple[str, str], TokenizersBackend] = {}
+
+
+def load(name: str, truncation_side: str = "left") -> TokenizersBackend:
+    """Load a tokenizer the way vLLM does, once per name and side."""
+    key = (name, truncation_side)
+    if key not in _loaded:
+        _loaded[key] = get_tokenizer(name, truncation_side=truncation_side)
+    return _loaded[key]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", QWEN_TOKENIZERS)
+def test_long_text_matches_normal_call(long_text: str, name: str):
+    tokenizer = load(name)
+    # The text must really be cut, or the comparison below proves nothing.
+    assert len(_cut_into_pieces(long_text)) > 40
+    expected = tokenizer(long_text, **NO_TRUNCATION)["input_ids"]
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, long_text, NO_TRUNCATION) == expected
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", QWEN_TOKENIZERS)
+def test_every_cut_place_is_a_token_boundary(name: str):
+    # Pieces of at least `PARALLEL_ENCODE_PIECE_CHARS` characters test only a
+    # few cut places. Cutting at all of them tests tens of thousands.
+    tokenizer = load(name)
+    text = make_text(MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS, seed=1)
+    cuts = [match.start() for match in _CUT_PATTERN.finditer(text)]
+    assert len(cuts) > 20_000
+    pieces = [text[a:b] for a, b in itertools.pairwise([0, *cuts, len(text)])]
+    expected = tokenizer(text, **NO_TRUNCATION)["input_ids"]
+    assert _encode_pieces(tokenizer, pieces) == expected
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", QWEN_TOKENIZERS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("side", ["left", "right"])
+def test_truncation_matches_normal_call(long_text: str, name: str, side: str):
+    tokenizer = load(name, truncation_side=side)
+    text = long_text[: 4 * MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS]
+    full = tokenizer(text, **NO_TRUNCATION)["input_ids"]
+
+    kwargs = {"truncation": True, "max_length": len(full) // 3}
+    expected = tokenizer(text, **kwargs)["input_ids"]
+    assert len(expected) == len(full) // 3
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, kwargs) == expected
+
+    # The normal call also truncates when only `max_length` is given.
+    kwargs = {"max_length": len(full) // 3}
+    assert tokenizer(text, **kwargs)["input_ids"] == expected
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, kwargs) == expected
+
+    # With truncation turned off, `max_length` does nothing.
+    kwargs = {"truncation": False, "max_length": len(full) // 3}
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, kwargs) == full
+
+    # vLLM passes one token more than the limit, so that a prompt that is too
+    # long still fails the length check. A prompt within the limit is kept.
+    kwargs = {"truncation": True, "max_length": len(full) + 1}
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, kwargs) == full
+
+
+def test_thread_pool_tokenizer_in_threads(long_text: str):
+    # HfRenderer wraps its tokenizer with `maybe_make_thread_pool` and calls
+    # it from several threads at the same time.
+    tokenizer = maybe_make_thread_pool(copy.deepcopy(load(QWEN_TOKENIZERS[0])), 2)
+    text = long_text[: 4 * MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS]
+    expected = tokenizer(text, **NO_TRUNCATION)["input_ids"]
+
+    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
+        results = list(
+            executor.map(
+                lambda _: try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, NO_TRUNCATION),
+                range(8),
+            )
+        )
+    assert all(result == expected for result in results)
+
+
+def test_normal_call_for_short_text_or_no_cut_place():
+    tokenizer = load(QWEN_TOKENIZERS[0])
+
+    short_text = make_text(MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS - 1000)
+    assert len(short_text) < MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, short_text, NO_TRUNCATION) is None
+
+    # CJK text has no space or line break in front of an ASCII letter or
+    # digit, and the only cut place below is too early to make two pieces.
+    for text in (
+        "中文分词测试" * MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS,
+        "x" * MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS,
+        "a b" + "中" * MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS,
+    ):
+        assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, NO_TRUNCATION) is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "kwargs",
+    [
+        {**NO_TRUNCATION, "return_offsets_mapping": True},
+        {**NO_TRUNCATION, "padding": "max_length"},
+        {"truncation": "only_first", "max_length": 10},
+        {"truncation": True, "max_length": None},
+        {"truncation": True, "max_length": 0},
+    ],
+)
+def test_normal_call_for_unsupported_arguments(kwargs: dict):
+    tokenizer = load(QWEN_TOKENIZERS[0])
+    text = make_text(MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS + 10_000)
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, kwargs) is None
+
+
+def _with_config(name: str, change) -> TokenizersBackend:
+    """Return a tokenizer built from the Rust configuration of `name` after
+    `change` edits the configuration in place."""
+    config = json.loads(load(name).backend_tokenizer.to_str())
+    change(config)
+    return TokenizersBackend(
+        tokenizer_object=Tokenizer.from_str(json.dumps(config)),
+        truncation_side="left",
+    )
+
+
+def _set_regex(regex: str):
+    def change(config):
+        config["pre_tokenizer"]["pretokenizers"][0]["pattern"]["Regex"] = regex
+
+    return change
+
+
+def _set(path: tuple, value):
+    def change(config):
+        node = config
+        for key in path[:-1]:
+            node = node[key]
+        node[path[-1]] = value
+
+    return change
+
+
+def _add_token(**fields):
+    def change(config):
+        token = {
+            "id": len(config["model"]["vocab"]) + 1000,
+            "content": "<|extra|>",
+            "single_word": False,
+            "lstrip": False,
+            "rstrip": False,
+            "normalized": False,
+            "special": True,
+        }
+        config["added_tokens"].append({**token, **fields})
+
+    return change
+
+
+def test_tokenizer_from_unchanged_config_is_supported():
+    # The tests below change one field of this configuration. Without the
+    # change, the tokenizer must be supported.
+    tokenizer = _with_config(QWEN_TOKENIZERS[0], lambda config: None)
+    text = make_text(MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS + 10_000)
+    token_ids = try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, NO_TRUNCATION)
+    assert token_ids is not None
+    assert token_ids == tokenizer(text, **NO_TRUNCATION)["input_ids"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "change",
+    [
+        # The regex of Llama 3 groups digits by three. It is not in the list.
+        _set_regex(
+            r"(?i:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)|[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?\p{L}+|\p{N}{1,3}"
+            r"| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]+[\r\n]*|\s*[\r\n]+|\s+(?!\S)|\s+"
+        ),
+        _set(("normalizer",), {"type": "Lowercase"}),
+        _set(("pre_tokenizer", "pretokenizers", 1, "add_prefix_space"), True),
+        _set(("model", "dropout"), 0.1),
+        _set(
+            ("post_processor",),
+            {
+                "type": "BertProcessing",
+                "cls": ["<|endoftext|>", 151643],
+                "sep": ["<|endoftext|>", 151643],
+            },
+        ),
+        _add_token(lstrip=True),
+        _add_token(single_word=True),
+        # A cut place inside the content of an added token.
+        _add_token(content="<|tool call|>"),
+        _add_token(content="<|line|>\nA"),
+    ],
+    ids=[
+        "llama3_regex",
+        "lowercase_normalizer",
+        "add_prefix_space",
+        "bpe_dropout",
+        "bert_post_processor",
+        "lstrip_token",
+        "single_word_token",
+        "token_with_space",
+        "token_with_line_break",
+    ],
+)
+def test_normal_call_for_unsupported_config(change):
+    tokenizer = _with_config(QWEN_TOKENIZERS[0], change)
+    text = make_text(MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS + 10_000)
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, NO_TRUNCATION) is None
+
+
+class _TokenInPythonTokenizer(TokenizersBackend):
+    """A tokenizer class that adds a token in Python, which the Rust
+    configuration does not show."""
+
+    def __call__(self, text, *args, add_special_tokens=True, **kwargs):
+        encoding = super().__call__(
+            text, *args, add_special_tokens=add_special_tokens, **kwargs
+        )
+        if add_special_tokens and isinstance(text, str):
+            encoding["input_ids"] = [0, *encoding["input_ids"]]
+        return encoding
+
+
+def test_normal_call_for_tokens_added_in_python():
+    config = load(QWEN_TOKENIZERS[0]).backend_tokenizer.to_str()
+    tokenizer = _TokenInPythonTokenizer(tokenizer_object=Tokenizer.from_str(config))
+    text = make_text(MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS + 10_000)
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, NO_TRUNCATION) is None
+
+
+class _KeepText:
+    """A pre-tokenizer step written in Python that leaves the text as it is."""
+
+    def pre_tokenize(self, pretok):
+        pass
+
+
+def test_normal_call_for_pre_tokenizer_in_python():
+    # A pre-tokenizer step written in Python cannot be serialized, so the
+    # configuration of the tokenizer cannot be checked.
+    tokenizer = _with_config(QWEN_TOKENIZERS[0], lambda config: None)
+    backend = tokenizer.backend_tokenizer
+    backend.pre_tokenizer = pre_tokenizers.Sequence(
+        [
+            pre_tokenizers.PreTokenizer.custom(_KeepText()),
+            backend.pre_tokenizer[0],
+            backend.pre_tokenizer[1],
+        ]
+    )
+    text = make_text(MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS + 10_000)
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, NO_TRUNCATION) is None
+
+
+def test_normal_call_for_other_tokenizers():
+    # GPT-2 splits text with the regex of its ByteLevel pre-tokenizer, which
+    # is not checked.
+    tokenizer = get_tokenizer("openai-community/gpt2")
+    text = make_text(MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS + 10_000)
+    assert try_parallel_encode(tokenizer, text, NO_TRUNCATION) is None

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tokenize a long prompt in pieces that are encoded in parallel.
+
+A Hugging Face fast tokenizer encodes a single text on one CPU thread. When it
+gets a list of texts, the Rust `tokenizers` library encodes them on all CPU
+threads. For the byte-level BPE tokenizers whose pre-tokenizer regex is in
+`_SPLIT_REGEXES`, a long text can be cut at places where the pre-tokenizer
+always ends one pre-token and starts the next one. The token IDs of the pieces,
+put one after the other, are then the token IDs of the whole text.
+"""
+
+import itertools
+import json
+import weakref
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Any, Final
+
+import regex as re
+from tokenizers import Tokenizer
+from tokenizers.models import BPE
+from transformers import TokenizersBackend
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+from .protocol import TokenizerLike
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# A prompt with fewer characters than this goes through the normal tokenizer
+# call. That is about 65k tokens of English text or code, which the normal
+# call encodes in about 50 ms, so a shorter prompt saves little.
+MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS: Final = 1 << 18
+
+# Each piece ends at the first cut place after this many characters.
+PARALLEL_ENCODE_PIECE_CHARS: Final = 1 << 16
+
+# The places where a text may be cut: before a space, or after a carriage
+# return or a line feed, where an ASCII letter or digit follows. With every
+# regex in `_SPLIT_REGEXES`, a pre-token ends at such a place and the next one
+# starts there. A space in front of a letter or digit always starts a
+# pre-token, and no alternative of the regexes runs from a line break into a
+# letter or digit. The regexes also find the same pre-tokens in a piece as in
+# the whole text. They have no lookbehind, and their one lookahead, `(?!\S)`
+# after a run of whitespace, sees a space in the whole text where the piece
+# ends. A run of whitespace that ends with a line break is matched by
+# `\s*[\r\n]+` before that lookahead is tried.
+_CUT_PATTERN: Final = re.compile(r"(?= [A-Za-z0-9])|(?<=[\r\n])(?=[A-Za-z0-9])")
+
+# The pre-tokenizer regexes for which the places in `_CUT_PATTERN` are known to
+# be pre-token boundaries.
+_SPLIT_REGEXES: Final = frozenset(
+    {
+        # Qwen2, Qwen2.5 and Qwen3.
+        (
+            r"(?i:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)|[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?\p{L}+|\p{N}"
+            r"| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{N}]+[\r\n]*|\s*[\r\n]+|\s+(?!\S)|\s+"
+        ),
+        # Qwen3.5 and later. Here a word can also contain combining marks.
+        (
+            r"(?i:'s|'t|'re|'ve|'m|'ll|'d)|[^\r\n\p{L}\p{N}]?[\p{L}\p{M}]+|\p{N}"
+            r"| ?[^\s\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}]+[\r\n]*|\s*[\r\n]+|\s+(?!\S)|\s+"
+        ),
+    }
+)
+
+# The keyword arguments of the normal tokenizer call that this module handles.
+_SUPPORTED_ENCODE_KWARGS: Final = frozenset(
+    {"add_special_tokens", "truncation", "max_length"}
+)
+
+# A short text with cut places of both kinds next to special tokens, digits,
+# a tab, a combining mark, CJK characters and an emoji. The normal call on this
+# text must give the same token IDs as its pieces.
+_SAMPLE_TEXT: Final = (
+    "<|im_start|>user\nA b\n\nC 1 23\r\nx\ty e\u0301 \u4e2d\u6587 \U0001f600 7"
+    "<|im_end|>\n"
+)
+
+# The result of `_supports_parallel_encode` for each tokenizer object. With
+# weak keys, a new tokenizer at a reused memory address does not get an old
+# result.
+_SUPPORTED_TOKENIZERS: Final[weakref.WeakKeyDictionary[TokenizersBackend, bool]] = (
+    weakref.WeakKeyDictionary()
+)
+
+
+def try_parallel_encode(
+    tokenizer: TokenizerLike,
+    text: str,
+    encode_kwargs: Mapping[str, Any],
+) -> list[int] | None:
+    """Encode `text` as pieces in parallel when the tokenizer allows it.
+
+    Args:
+        tokenizer: The tokenizer of the renderer.
+        text: The text prompt.
+        encode_kwargs: The keyword arguments of the normal tokenizer call.
+
+    Returns:
+        The token IDs of `tokenizer(text, **encode_kwargs)`, or `None` when
+        `text` has fewer than `MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS` characters or no
+        place to cut, or when the tokenizer or the arguments are not
+        supported. The caller then makes the normal call.
+
+    """
+    if len(text) < MIN_PARALLEL_ENCODE_CHARS:
+        return None
+    if not isinstance(tokenizer, TokenizersBackend):
+        return None
+    if not encode_kwargs.keys() <= _SUPPORTED_ENCODE_KWARGS:
+        return None
+
+    max_length = encode_kwargs.get("max_length")
+    truncation = encode_kwargs.get("truncation")
+    # The normal call also truncates when only `max_length` is given.
+    if truncation is None:
+        truncation = max_length is not None
+    side = tokenizer.truncation_side
+    if truncation is False:
+        max_length = None
+    elif (
+        truncation is not True
+        or not isinstance(max_length, int)
+        or max_length <= 0
+        or side not in ("left", "right")
+    ):
+        # A truncation strategy given by name and truncation to the default
+        # length of the model are not handled.
+        return None
+
+    if not _supports_parallel_encode(tokenizer):
+        return None
+
+    pieces = _cut_into_pieces(text)
+    if len(pieces) < 2:
+        return None
+
+    token_ids = _encode_pieces(tokenizer, pieces)
+
+    # Like the normal call, keep the first or the last `max_length` token IDs,
+    # depending on the truncation side of the tokenizer.
+    if max_length is not None and len(token_ids) > max_length:
+        if side == "left":
+            del token_ids[:-max_length]
+        else:
+            del token_ids[max_length:]
+    return token_ids
+
+
+def _cut_into_pieces(text: str) -> list[str]:
+    """Cut `text` into pieces of at least `PARALLEL_ENCODE_PIECE_CHARS`
+    characters, each one ending at a place in `_CUT_PATTERN`. The last piece
+    can be shorter."""
+    starts = [0]
+    while (
+        match := _CUT_PATTERN.search(text, starts[-1] + PARALLEL_ENCODE_PIECE_CHARS)
+    ) is not None:
+        starts.append(match.start())
+    return [text[a:b] for a, b in itertools.pairwise([*starts, len(text)])]
+
+
+def _encode_pieces(tokenizer: TokenizersBackend, pieces: list[str]) -> list[int]:
+    """Encode `pieces` in one call and return their token IDs one after the
+    other."""
+    # A list of texts goes to `encode_batch` of the Rust tokenizer, which
+    # encodes the texts on all CPU threads. Special tokens are off because a
+    # supported tokenizer adds none, which `_supports_parallel_encode` checks.
+    encoding = tokenizer(pieces, add_special_tokens=False, return_attention_mask=False)
+    return list(itertools.chain.from_iterable(encoding["input_ids"]))
+
+
+def _supports_parallel_encode(tokenizer: TokenizersBackend) -> bool:
+    """Whether pieces cut at `_CUT_PATTERN` give the token IDs of the whole
+    text with `tokenizer`. Each tokenizer object is checked once."""
+    supported = _SUPPORTED_TOKENIZERS.get(tokenizer)
+    if supported is None:
+        supported = _has_supported_config(tokenizer) and _matches_normal_call(tokenizer)
+        _SUPPORTED_TOKENIZERS[tokenizer] = supported
+        logger.debug(
+            "Long prompts are %s in parallel pieces with the tokenizer %s.",
+            "tokenized" if supported else "not tokenized",
+            tokenizer.name_or_path,
+        )
+    return supported
+
+
+def _has_supported_config(tokenizer: TokenizersBackend) -> bool:
+    """Whether the configuration of the Rust tokenizer makes every place in
+    `_CUT_PATTERN` a place where the token IDs of a text can be split."""
+    backend = tokenizer.backend_tokenizer
+    # A replacement backend, such as the fastokens shim, is not checked.
+    if not isinstance(backend, Tokenizer):
+        return False
+    try:
+        normalizer = _component_config(backend.normalizer)
+        pre_tokenizer = _component_config(backend.pre_tokenizer) or {}
+        post_processor = _component_config(backend.post_processor)
+    except Exception:
+        # A component that is written in Python cannot be serialized.
+        logger.debug("Cannot read the tokenizer configuration.", exc_info=True)
+        return False
+
+    # NFC never joins a space, an ASCII letter or an ASCII digit with the
+    # character in front of it, so it does not change the text across a cut
+    # place. Other normalizers are not checked.
+    if normalizer is not None and normalizer.get("type") != "NFC":
+        return False
+
+    steps = pre_tokenizer.get("pretokenizers") or []
+    if pre_tokenizer.get("type") != "Sequence" or len(steps) != 2:
+        return False
+    split, byte_level = steps
+    if (
+        split.get("type") != "Split"
+        or (split.get("pattern") or {}).get("Regex") not in _SPLIT_REGEXES
+        or split.get("behavior") != "Isolated"
+        or split.get("invert")
+    ):
+        return False
+    # The byte-level step must not add a space at the start of each piece and
+    # must not split the text again with its own regex.
+    if (
+        byte_level.get("type") != "ByteLevel"
+        or byte_level.get("add_prefix_space")
+        or byte_level.get("use_regex")
+    ):
+        return False
+
+    # BPE dropout picks merges at random, so the same text can get other IDs.
+    if not isinstance(backend.model, BPE) or backend.model.dropout:
+        return False
+
+    # A post-processor that adds special tokens would add them to every piece.
+    # The byte-level post-processor only changes offsets.
+    if post_processor is not None and post_processor.get("type") != "ByteLevel":
+        return False
+
+    # Added tokens are found in the raw text before the pre-tokenizer runs.
+    # A cut place inside the content of an added token could split one of
+    # its occurrences, and an added token that strips whitespace or needs
+    # word boundaries looks at the text on the other side of a cut place.
+    # The search starts at the second character, because a cut place in front
+    # of an added token does not split it.
+    for token in backend.get_added_tokens_decoder().values():
+        if (
+            token.lstrip
+            or token.rstrip
+            or token.single_word
+            or _CUT_PATTERN.search(token.content, 1) is not None
+        ):
+            return False
+    return True
+
+
+def _component_config(component: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    """Return the configuration of a normalizer, pre-tokenizer or
+    post-processor of a Rust tokenizer, as it is written in `tokenizer.json`.
+    Unlike `Tokenizer.to_str`, this does not write the vocabulary, which takes
+    about 100 ms for a Qwen tokenizer."""
+    if component is None:
+        return None
+    return json.loads(component.__getstate__())
+
+
+def _matches_normal_call(tokenizer: TokenizersBackend) -> bool:
+    """Whether the normal call on `_SAMPLE_TEXT` gives the token IDs of the
+    sample cut at every place in `_CUT_PATTERN`, with and without special
+    tokens. This catches a tokenizer class that changes the text or adds
+    tokens in Python before the Rust tokenizer runs."""
+    cuts = [match.start() for match in _CUT_PATTERN.finditer(_SAMPLE_TEXT)]
+    pieces = [
+        _SAMPLE_TEXT[a:b]
+        for a, b in itertools.pairwise([0, *cuts, len(_SAMPLE_TEXT)])
+        if a < b
+    ]
+    expected = _encode_pieces(tokenizer, pieces)
+    return all(
+        list(tokenizer(_SAMPLE_TEXT, add_special_tokens=add)["input_ids"]) == expected
+        for add in (True, False)
+    )

issue_comments.body: This is already what fastokens does

I checked `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` with fastokens 0.3.4 on the 1M-token prompt of this PR. It also cuts the prompt at pre-token boundaries and encodes the chunks in parallel, its token IDs are the same for Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-0.8B, and it is faster than this PR at every prompt length in the description. So I am closing this PR.

The fastokens package is not in the vLLM Docker images, so `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` raises an ImportError there (#47855). Is there a plan to add it? #47859 and #47863 got no review.
@maeehart yes I think we can get it added to the image by default.
